resources.string: Resolution the PC sends. More pixels mean more detail and load.
Frames per second the PC sends. Match your display.
Video bitrate in Mbps. Too high stutters on a weak link. Stream menu → Bitrate: this stream only.
Bitrate on a metered network (mobile data, some hotspots). 0 uses a quarter of the normal bitrate.
Warp modes may not work on every device.
MediaCodec callbacks instead of polling. H.264, HEVC and AV1 only. Turn off if decoding is unstable.
Balanced pacing that polls the decoder more often. Overrides other MediaCodec pacing except Fast V-Sync. Device-dependent.
Extra MediaCodec low-latency options. Gain depends on chip and driver. Turn off if video is unstable.
Asks Vibepollo or Apollo for a virtual PC display at the requested resolution and FPS. Needs host support.
Starts the stream in the device\'s current portrait or landscape orientation. The PC desktop is not rotated.
Swaps width and height for a portrait stream (1080 × 1920). Needs Auto Orientation and host support.
Aligns a stream that does not fill the screen to the top center instead of the middle.
Scales the host virtual display: at 150%%, 1920 × 1080 renders as 2880 × 1620 on the PC. Costs PC GPU.
Local picture fit only.
Adds a resolution to Video resolution: enter width x height (1920x1080), then select it there.
Sets the bitrate in Mbps; decimals and values above the slider\'s range allowed. Also updates Video bitrate.
Adds a custom FPS (decimals allowed) to Video frame rate; select it there. Host, game and display limit the result.
Asks Android firmly to use the selected display mode. Helps if refresh-rate requests are ignored; may misbehave on some firmware.
Requests HDR video. Needs game, host GPU, decoder and display support (10-bit HEVC, AV1 or PyroWave).
Shows the stream and menu on an attached monitor or TV at the configured resolution and FPS. The handheld controls the menu.
Upscales a lower-resolution stream to the display size, or only sharpens it (Mode). Costs GPU time. Menu changes last one session.
4:4:4 costs bandwidth and GPU.
Reconstruction method. All add GPU work.
Final sharpening. 0 disables it, not SGSR 1 reconstruction. In Sharpen only it is the whole effect. Menu changes last one session.
Internal size when the stream already matches the display. Menu changes last one session.
Channels the PC sends. Surround needs matching playback.
Lets Android\'s system equalizer and effects process stream audio. May add delay.
Plays game audio on the PC as well as here. Turn off to keep the PC speakers quiet.
Positive values ignore small stick movement near center (drift). Negative values offset a controller\'s own dead zone.
Reports gamepads as they connect or disconnect. When off, one gamepad always stays present, for games that need one at launch.
Uses the Delos USB driver for Xbox and Nintendo Pro controllers Android cannot handle natively. May ask for USB permission.
Lets the USB driver also claim controllers Android supports natively. Needs the USB driver. A workaround.
Hold Start during a stream to switch the gamepad between game input and mouse emulation.
Stick that scrolls in gamepad mouse mode.
Swaps A/B and X/Y for gamepad input and on-screen controls (Nintendo layout). Not Delos navigation.
Always uses a controller\'s touchpad as a PC mouse. Off lets supported hosts receive native touchpad input.
Lets the PC read an external gamepad\'s gyroscope and accelerometer. Needs Android 12 or newer. Turn off if no game uses motion, to save a little power and traffic.
Uses this device\'s own gyroscope and accelerometer when the gamepad has none or Android cannot read them. The PC may then see a PlayStation controller.
Uses the built-in sensors even if the external gamepad has working ones. Needs Built-in device gyroscope.

Steadies gyro aiming. 0 is off. Higher values remove more jitter but add a little delay to slow movement; fast flicks stay responsive. Applies to the next stream; the stream menu (More) changes it live.
Compatibility path for Joy-Cons with missing or misrecognized buttons. Leave off if they work.
Reports gamepad battery status to the host. Turn off if battery polling coincides with touch or mouse stutter.
Sends host rumble to supported gamepads. Controller, connection and driver decide which effects work.
How game rumble feels. Next stream.
Uses the handheld\'s vibration motor for game rumble when the gamepad cannot. Needs a vibration motor.
Uses the handheld\'s vibration motor even when a controller supports rumble. Not for the built-in USB driver.
Strength of this device\'s vibration for game rumble. Needs amplitude control. Not interface haptics.
How touch becomes PC input. Stream menu: this session only.
Saves mouse-mode changes made in a stream. When off, they last only that stream.
Shows Android\'s pointer for a physical mouse instead of hiding it. Not the cursor the PC draws in the video.
In multi-touch mode: three fingers open the system keyboard, four the full keyboard, five the stream menu.
Forwards a physical mouse\'s Back and Forward buttons to the PC. Turn off if right-click or navigation misbehaves.
Absolute positioning instead of relative game movement. Suits remote desktop; many games need relative input.
Horizontal sensitivity of a physical trackpad. Larger moves farther; negative reverses.
Vertical sensitivity of a physical trackpad. Larger moves farther; negative reverses.
Vibrates when a hold starts drag-and-drop on supported Samsung trackpads. Not for ordinary clicks.
Hold time on a supported Samsung trackpad before a drag starts. Shorter may start unwanted drags.
Swaps horizontal and vertical trackpad input for devices that report a rotated trackpad. Leave off if movement is right.
Uses QWERTY key translation for stream input. Turn off for another layout with a compatible host.
Sends Right Alt as the Mac Command key, including combinations. Left Alt is unchanged. For streaming a Mac.
Ignores synthetic Android input events. Stops stray keys from buggy drivers but blocks soft-keyboard input.
Forwards text from swipe typing and dictation in chunks. Good on the desktop; some games expect single key presses.
Uploads this device\'s clipboard when the stream starts or regains focus; fetches the PC\'s when it loses focus. Needs Vibepollo or Apollo.
Shows a brief message when automatic clipboard transfer succeeds or fails. Does not enable synchronization.
Marks clipboard content from the PC as sensitive so Android hides its preview. Does not encrypt or disable transfer.
Opacity of the full on-screen keyboard. Separate from virtual gamepad opacity.
Turns off automatic fitting of the full keyboard so the saved width, height and alignment apply.
Height of the full on-screen keyboard when automatic fitting is off. Taller: larger keys, more of the game covered.
Width of the full on-screen keyboard when automatic fitting is off. Keep it reachable on your screen.
Horizontal anchor of the manually sized full keyboard.
Keeps virtual Shift, Ctrl, Alt and similar modifiers active after a tap, so combinations can be typed one key at a time.
Hides on-screen connection-quality warnings during streaming. Statistics stay.
Saves the stream\'s zoom and pan for later sessions. When off, adjustments last only that stream.
Keeps the stream in Picture-in-Picture while multitasking. View only: no game control in the small window.
Shows the virtual gamepad over the stream for touch play. The stream menu toggles it for the session.
Hides the virtual gamepad while Android detects a physical controller; it returns when the controller disconnects.
Local vibration when pressing virtual gamepad buttons. Touch feedback, not game rumble. Needs a vibration motor.
Shows only the virtual L3 and R3 stick-click buttons instead of the full gamepad.
Adds the Guide/Home button to the virtual gamepad; its action depends on host and platform.
Opacity of the virtual gamepad and custom special-key controls. Separate from full-keyboard opacity.
Lets virtual stick centers move within their interaction area instead of staying fixed.
Visibility of the free virtual stick\'s background while idle. Low keeps the picture clearer; high is easier to find.
Restores this profile\'s virtual gamepad to default sizes and positions at once. Other profiles are kept.
Shows the custom special-key layer over the stream, using the layout selected below. Separate from the full keyboard.
Hides the built-in key combinations from the stream menu\'s Send keys, leaving your imported commands.
Local vibration when tapping custom on-screen keyboard buttons; not game rumble. Needs a vibration motor.
Active one of this profile\'s five special-key layouts.
Draws custom special-key buttons as squares instead of circles. The keys sent are unchanged.
Restores the selected special-key layout to defaults at once. Other layouts and profiles are kept.
Replaces the selected special-key layout with a file from Android\'s picker. Export first for a backup.
Saves the selected special-key layout to a file, as a backup or for another device.
Extra sensitivity scaling for touchscreen game input, set by the axis sliders below. The stream menu toggles it live.
Applies touch sensitivity to the whole screen; when off, only to the right half, leaving the left for movement controls.
Recenters scaled touch coordinates that run past the screen edge so high-sensitivity drags can continue.
Horizontal sensitivity of multi-touch game input; higher turns small finger movement into larger in-game movement.
Vertical sensitivity of multi-touch game input; higher turns small finger movement into larger in-game movement.
Horizontal pointer sensitivity for touchscreen trackpad mode and custom virtual touchpads.
Vertical pointer sensitivity for touchscreen trackpad mode and custom virtual touchpads.
Shows FPS, 1%% low FPS, bitrate, packet loss and latency. Total latency is not button-to-screen. The stream menu cycles full, compact, off.
Shows one compact statistics line at the top center instead of the full panel. The stream menu cycles full, compact, off.
Codec the PC encodes with; host and decoder must support it.
Shows frame-rate choices above the display\'s detected capability. Raises host load; refresh rate is unchanged.
Lets Android choose a lower display refresh rate when suitable. Saves power but can slow presentation.
Requests full-range video levels instead of limited range. Enable only if host and display agree, or blacks and highlights crush.
Sends a small control packet about every 20 ms to discourage Wi-Fi power saving. May help device-specific loss.
Language of stream messages and system screens. The Delos shell and its help stay English.
Imports custom key combinations for Send keys and the special-key controls, replacing this profile\'s custom commands.
Opens instructions for the custom-key file format. Load the resulting file with Import Custom Keys.
Opens device and controller diagnostics without a stream: device details, controller IDs and sensors, vibration test, control preview.
Keeps a rolling log (2 MB at most) of events and errors on this device. Nothing leaves it unless you share it from Debug info, with names and addresses removed. Off stops new lines.
Takes three colors from the selected game\'s cover for the animated background; falls back to PC artwork. Needs Material You off.
Shows the newest frame at once; may stutter.
Matches frames to the display refresh with a small queue.
Balanced; asks the host for fewer frames near refresh.
Steady delivery; adds buffering and latency.
Requests twice the FPS (60 → 120); shows the newest frame.
Requests four times the FPS (60 → 240).
Syncs to the lower of FPS and refresh. MediaCodec only.
Picks H.264 or HEVC. AV1 and PyroWave need selecting.
Efficient at low bitrates. Needs AV1 encode on the host and decode here.
Less bandwidth than H.264; supports 10-bit HDR. May fall back.
Broadest compatibility; needs more bandwidth. No HDR.
GPU wavelet codec with its own Vulkan decoder. Needs a fast link and far higher bitrate.
Half-resolution color. Cheapest.
Full color. Uses 4:2:0 if the host cannot.
Edge reconstruction from the current frame. Cheapest.
A stronger spatial filter on the current frame.
Delos SGSR 2 for video: motion from optical flow.
SGSR2-DV plus a mask that rejects stale detail. Most GPU.
No scaling; sharpens at stream size. Costs little GPU.
Renders 1080p at 2560 × 1440.
Renders 1080p at 3840 × 2160. Costs more GPU time and memory.
Whole picture; black bars if aspect ratios differ.
Fills the screen; crops if aspect ratios differ.
Fills the screen without cropping; the picture distorts.
Two channels for handheld speakers and most headphones.
Six channels. Needs a 5.1 playback path.
Eight channels. Use Stereo if channels are missing.
The game\'s rumble exactly as it sends it.
A weaker, rounded rumble.
A strong short kick at the start of each rumble, then the normal level.
A slow pulsed rumble that feels deeper.
Values edited under About → Debug info.
Neither stick scrolls.
The right stick scrolls.
The left stick scrolls.
Direct multi-touch; the host must support touch.
Touch a point to point or click there.
Relative pointer movement; used for external displays.
Relative movement for mouse-style games.
No touch input; stylus and edge swipe still work.
Direct touch with the mouse buttons swapped.
Anchored to the left edge.
Centered horizontally.
Anchored to the right edge.
Requests a %1$s stream.
Requests %1$s FPS. Warp modes multiply it.
Follows the Android language.
Uses this language where translations exist.
Import, export and reset act on this layout.
The saved choice is unavailable
PyroWave recommends %1$d Mbps here.
LFR is enabled: Balanced used.
Fast V-Sync overrides LFR.
Not used with PyroWave.
Needs the PyroWave codec.
HDR is on: 4:2:0 used.
PyroWave offers all five modes
Not used by Sharpen only.
Closes this menu and continues the stream.
Opens or closes the Delos on-screen keyboard: D-pad moves, A types, B closes. Not Android\'s system keyboard (More).
Cycles full statistics, compact statistics, off. 1%% low FPS covers the slowest frames of about ten seconds.
Adjusts this device\'s brightness for this stream; the system setting returns afterwards.
Changes this device\'s screen brightness now; the system setting returns afterwards. Not the PC or a monitor.
Requests a new video bitrate without reconnecting. Needs Vibepollo; the host may cap it. Lasts for this stream.
Sends the requested bitrate to Vibepollo. The accepted value can be lower. Saved defaults are unchanged.
Upscales a low-resolution stream, or supersamples a native one. Costs GPU time; applies live and is kept for this game.
Turns the upscaler, or Sharpen only, on or off for this stream; the picture may flicker.
Renders a native-resolution stream at a larger size, then reduces it. Costs GPU time; lasts for this stream.
Renders at a larger internal size. Costs GPU time.
For 1080p: 1.33× renders at 2560 × 1440, 2× at 3840 × 2160 and costs more GPU time and memory.
Applies live. Switching to or from Sharpen only may flicker.
Final sharpening. 0 disables it, not SGSR 1 reconstruction. In Sharpen only it is the whole effect. Lasts for this stream.
More stream controls: clipboard, host commands, key combinations, zoom, touch and on-screen controls. Actions run at once.
Stops streaming and returns to the Delos library. The game keeps running on the PC.
Asks the host to end the running application, then disconnects. Runs at once, so save first.
Sends a built-in or imported key combination to the PC once; the menu closes. Import custom ones under Controls.
Copies this device\'s clipboard to the PC once. Needs Vibepollo or Apollo clipboard support.
Fetches the PC clipboard to this device once. Needs Vibepollo or Apollo clipboard support.
Lists server commands configured in Vibepollo or Apollo. The host decides what each does.
Sends Ctrl + Shift + Esc to the PC, which opens Task Manager on Windows.
Toggles the stream\'s zoom-and-pan controls. Local view only; Remember Zoom & Pan decides whether it persists.
Chooses how touch controls the PC: direct touch, trackpad or off. Remember mouse mode decides whether it persists.
Shows or hides Android\'s pointer for a physical mouse during this stream. Not the PC cursor in the video.
Shows or hides the virtual gamepad during this stream. Opacity and layout are set under Controls.
Opens or closes Android\'s system keyboard, after closing this menu. Not the Delos keyboard (the Keyboard tile).
Toggles extra touchscreen sensitivity scaling, configured in settings.
Steadies gyro aiming at once, kept for this game. 0 is off. More smoothing adds a little delay to slow movement.
Needs External gamepad gyroscope or Built-in device gyroscope turned on in Settings; applies from the next stream.
Picks how host rumble feels, at once and saved. Stays open: pick again to compare. B goes back.
Sends %1$s to the PC once, then returns to the stream.
Runs the host-defined command %1$s on the PC at once. Set in Vibepollo or Apollo.
